releases.title: More room for every card
releases.summary: Cards are easier to move and read on phones, room chat stays tucked below the table, and every device gets a clearer way to install.
details: Drag a card directly from its body. A separate information button now stays in the top-right corner, while the point badge keeps its own space at top-left.
Timeline information buttons are anchored inside their cards, and room chat becomes a compact full-width drawer below the play surface on phones.
Home and Downloads now recognize Android, iPhone, iPad, Windows, macOS, and Linux, with the right install guidance or recommended desktop format shown first.
The first 50-card artwork research batch is ready for human review. Unapproved images are not published, so every pending card continues to use its existing category artwork.

releases.title: The shared table stays steady
releases.summary: Multiplayer plays confirm sooner, and room chat now has a quiet dock that stays clear of the cards.
details: Card moves now reach the shared room as soon as the placement animation begins, so a flourish cannot delay a move past its turn or lose a race with a timeout.
Older timeout and room responses can no longer roll a newer multiplayer board backward or show a timeout reveal for a card that landed.
Open room chat from the game header. The expanded conversation sits below the timeline and hand, while multiplayer games keep ads off the play surface.
Age setup asks players to choose a month and year instead of pre-filling a date that could mistakenly classify a 13-year-old as under 13.

releases.title: A table closer to the vision
releases.summary: The Modern gameplay table brings portrait cards, parchment and a leather hand tray into a more balanced composition.
details: The timeline sits directly on the map, with brass navigation and larger dashed placement targets when a card is selected.
Your hand uses taller cards, round value badges and a centered leather tray. Long titles remain readable.
Classic/Modern and version controls now take their own space in the header, so they cannot float over scores and hearts.
Classic customization and the whole-hand layout remain available. Official event illustrations are a separate work in progress.

releases.title: A clearer table for every turn
releases.summary: The Modern gameplay table now gives the timeline and your whole hand a warmer, clearer place to play. Version and changelog controls stay close at hand.
details: Modern gameplay uses a full-width parchment timeline, framed cards, a stitched leather hand tray and more readable scores and dates.
A single view-switch control in the gameplay top bar lets you move between Classic and Modern without ending the game.
The version number opens What’s new from the Modern Home and both gameplay views. The staff console also has a themed changelog control.
The whole-hand, touch, keyboard, controller and large-text fallback behavior remains in place. Individual event illustrations are still under editorial review.

releases.title: A richer table, made for the moment
releases.summary: Modern Time Chronicles opens on a warm parchment table with leather panels, brass controls, and a rebuilt main menu. Your Classic table and its saved colors are still here whenever you want them.
details: The Modern main menu brings the illustrated desktop and mobile designs to life, with a brass Quick Play control, stitched leather play panel, saved-run resume, and a community board.
Modern is now the default view, with curated parchment light and deep-leather dark appearances that follow your device when you choose System.
Switch between Modern and Classic from Home, Settings, or while you play. The switch only changes presentation, so your game, selected card, and editor draft stay put.

Cards and gameplay use the new framed treatment while keeping titles, clues, dates, controls, and screen-reader information as clear text. Individual historical card illustrations are coming in a later artwork release.
Custom cards can use library artwork or a PNG, JPEG, or WebP from your device. Images are normalized and kept in device storage; full deck exports carry the artwork with them.
The table still protects the whole hand: four standard cards and the timeline stay together, larger hands navigate inside their tray, and large text can always scroll instead of losing a card.

releases.title: Your whole hand, back at the table
releases.summary: All four cards fit together on phones and desktops. Larger hands scroll with clear navigation, and the timeline stays within reach.
details: The table makes room for your hand first, with two rows on phones and four cards across on larger screens.
Long timelines have a full overview and readable cards you can scroll or jump through.
Larger hands show a card range with Previous and Next controls, alongside normal scrolling.
Touch the card to select it, or use its Drag handle to move it. Ordinary swipes scroll without playing a card.
Menu holds Customize and audio settings; chapter details and advertisements stay below the playing area. Enlarged text and short screens can always scroll.

releases.title: The table stays in reach
releases.summary: Keyboard and controller play now move real focus and activate real game controls, while the timeline and hand share one compact play surface.
details: Your first arrow or directional-pad press now enters the active hand or timeline, even when nothing had focus before.
Standard controllers use the same guarded actions as keyboard and pointer play, including region changes, a real game-menu action, held-input timing, and neutral reconnects.
Practice, local, and online tables keep the timeline, hand, and required actions together, with internal scrolling for longer timelines and hands.
Hidden tabs pause nonessential update, live-operations, support, and catalog refresh work while multiplayer recovery and turn state continue to use their existing safeguards.

releases.title: A clearer table for every player
releases.summary: Light and dark themes now stay readable, updates stay out of the way, and keyboard or controller play is ready.
details: The refreshed Customize panel keeps its close button visible while you scroll, and color defaults stay correct when the device switches between light and dark mode.
What’s new opens on request with the latest release first and older updates behind Previous updates. New players no longer receive automatic announcement popups.
Menus and games accept arrow keys, Enter, Space, Escape, and standard browser gamepads.
The transfer page now uses the same Time Chronicles header and visual language as the game.

releases.title: Plus is wired up and verified
releases.summary: The Store's Plus plans are connected end to end with setup checks that fail closed, and the changelog always finishes loading.
details: Plus monthly, Plus annual, and Lifetime Plus now report as purchasable only when a real, mode-specific Stripe key is installed, so an example or placeholder value can never make the Store look open for business.

A new setup check verifies the Stripe account, every configured price, the signed webhook endpoint, and the customer portal before paid checkout is switched on, and names exactly what is still missing.
The subscription catalog documents and validates the annual plan alongside monthly and lifetime, including the staff price settings that quote every plan.

The changelog can no longer wait forever on "Loading the latest changelog…": every release-notes request now has a deadline and always reaches its content, or its clear retry state. Release notes also revalidate instead of serving a stale copy from the previous release.
Ownership rules stay the same: earned and individually purchased packs remain yours, Plus covers every released pack while it is paid, and Lifetime Plus keeps them permanently.

releases.title: Staff invitations arrive safely
releases.summary: Staff invitations now survive refreshes, send through a durable email queue, and explain sign-in problems clearly.
details: Invitation links move into a short-lived secure server session before the URL fragment is cleared, so refreshes and canceled Google sign-ins can be retried safely.
Account creation and invitation acceptance are transactional, pending usernames are reserved, and concurrent acceptance cannot create duplicate staff accounts.
Invitations send through encrypted queued email jobs with bounded retries, delivery status, secure copy-link fallback, resend rotation, and revoke controls.
Staff login now gives actionable messages for expired invitations, wrong accounts, canceled Google sign-ins, provider failures, and username conflicts.

releases.title: Plus, your way
releases.summary: Choose free play, a flexible Plus plan, lifetime access, or a permanent pack purchase, with points still in play.
details: Time Chronicles Plus is priced at $2.99 monthly, $24.99 yearly, or $59.99 once for lifetime access. Annual billing is about $2.08 per month, around 30% less than monthly.
Earn eligible released packs with the existing point system or buy a single pack permanently for $0.99. Earned and purchased packs stay yours if a subscription ends.

Paid purchases are prepared for verified Stripe Checkout, while existing subscriptions keep their current renewal price. Stripe purchases remain paused until provider tests, production setup, and launch checks are complete.
Weekly community releases keep their own permanent identity and retained content, so rotating the weekly selection does not replace an owned release.
Staff sales and subscription views add date ranges, personal saved views, financial totals and private CSV, XLSX and PDF reports. Billing management remains subject to release verification.

releases.title: Welcome back to the staff table
releases.summary: Staff sign-in is restored after the move, gifts are easier to send, and room hosting gets leaner.
details: Google staff sign-in now returns to the new website. Staff passwords, invitations, permissions, and authenticator checks remain protected.
Staff can check a guest recipient before giving points, a permanent pack, or a 1, 7, or 30-day pack trial. Players do not need a new login.
Room requests read their own table instead of scanning every room. Background housekeeping clears abandoned rooms even when the lobby is quiet.
Peer-hosting recovery and concurrent-room simulations have expanded coverage. Public peer tables remain disabled while relay and device testing are completed.

releases.title: More room to play
releases.summary: A slimmer table, lasting heart containers, fresh cards through every chapter, and the Earliest First challenge.
details: The desktop sidebar takes less space, while mobile tables and compact result views keep cards and the next action readable. Optional card details and final replays expand in place.
Lost hearts leave empty containers. Revealed and attempted cards never return during a game, including later Quick Play chapters.
Earliest First challenges you to choose the earliest year in your hand before placing it. Equal years can be played in either order, locally or online.
Desktop download links open once. Linux startup includes a compatibility fix for blank windows on affected graphics drivers.

releases.title: The timeline keeps moving
releases.summary: Successful placements can celebrate inline, desktop stakes are easier to read, and the player experience speaks more naturally.
details: Successful placement popups remain available by default, but players can turn future success popups off from the reveal or Settings; misses, timeouts, handoffs, and final results still pause when they need attention.

The faster setting celebrates correct cards directly on the timeline with a check, visible score gain, and a small particle burst, then advances once after a readable 800-millisecond beat with a static reduced-motion path.
Desktop score rails now give points, streaks, and hearts more size, contrast, and active-player emphasis in local and online games without exposing hidden totals.

Home, setup, practice, gameplay, results, settings, decks, store, support, social, downloads, audio, and update copy now use a clearer game-night voice while sourced facts and trust-sensitive wording stay intact.

releases.title: Every pack stays on theme
releases.summary: Weekly packs now prioritize cards related to their winning idea, How to Play becomes an animated practice table, and staff gain complete pack and promotional-access controls.
details: Food on the Move and every future weekly winner now draw all matching-category cards first in deterministic order, using unrelated fallback cards only when the sourced catalog cannot fill fifty positions.
Every shipped deck is covered by the strict 50-card source and category audit, while staff can create managed packs or edit and publish an override for any built-in pack from Pack Studio.

How to Play is now a full, visible practice screen with a mock hand, placement slots, directional arrows, drag motion, reveal feedback, and reduced-motion support instead of a blocking tutorial popup.

Authorized staff can grant a pack to one player permanently or until a chosen expiration, or schedule labeled all-account pack promotions with optional start and end times; production and local multiplayer enforce the same live access rules.

releases.title: Subscriber packs open online tables
releases.summary: Hosts can now use packs covered by a verified subscription, lifetime unlock, current-pack unlock, or individual pack purchase when creating and managing online rooms.
details: Room creation and pack offers carry the device's private billing recovery proof to the server, where durable provider records—not client entitlement flags—determine pack access.
Active subscriptions, lifetime access, and verified current-pack support unlock every active catalog pack for online play, including Cryptids & Mysterious Events.
Verified individual pack purchases grant that exact pack online, while unknown and inactive packs remain unavailable unless explicitly purchased.

releases.title: Online turns hold steady through the unknown
releases.summary: Hosted pack choices now survive setup and reconnects, network-retried card plays are idempotent, and fifty sourced cryptid and mystery moments join the catalog.
details: Room creation carries the host's exact pack snapshot into the authoritative lobby and repairs a mismatched response before the table can start; locked selections now produce a clear error instead of silently becoming Foundations.
Automatic rejoin signals are consumed once, ending the host-side reconnect loop that could leave the waiting-room action stuck on Saving.
Each online placement keeps one durable request id across retries, so a move accepted before its response is lost is returned as the same move rather than appearing to revert or requiring a replay.
Cryptids & Mysterious Events adds 50 sourced cards spanning legendary creatures, strange signals, disappearances, investigations, and famous hoaxes.

releases.title: Hosted tables keep their chosen packs
releases.summary: Pack selections now carry into online hosting and remain synchronized while the host adjusts the waiting room.
details: Online host setup starts with the packs already selected by the player instead of resetting to Foundations.
The room's authoritative pack list is synchronized back to the player selection after creation and every pre-game host edit.
Selections that are unavailable for online play are safely filtered while valid unlocked packs remain selected.

releases.title: Fire, motion, and companionship join the timeline
releases.summary: Volcano history, transportation milestones, and the story of household pets arrive as three new sourced packs.
details: Fire Mountains adds 50 sourced cards spanning ancient eruptions, famous disasters, newborn islands, scientific breakthroughs, aviation hazards, and modern preparedness.
Wheels Through Time adds 50 sourced cards tracing transport from the first wheel and ancient roads through bicycles, cars, trains, ships, aircraft, spacecraft, and autonomous vehicles.
Furry & Feathered adds 50 sourced cards about dogs, cats, birds, rabbits, fish, and other companions across domestication, veterinary care, service, science, film, and internet culture.
All three packs are available in the player catalog, unlockable with points, highlighted as new releases, and projected into authoritative multiplayer rooms.

releases.title: Three new stories arrive at the table
releases.summary: Toy-industry building history, food history, and cartoon milestones join the catalog alongside new-release discovery and a server-authorized custom pack creator.
details: Brick by Brick, Food History, and Cartoon Milestones each add 50 sourced, unique cards with balanced difficulty and complete server-side multiplayer projections.

Built-in releases, weekly community winners, and staff-published packs now share one release clock: players see a one-time arrival popup, and packs remain highlighted at the top of catalog views for seven days.
The separate custom pack screen lets players configure and validate at least nine cards before saving; canceling the draft never spends points.
Verified supporters create custom packs without spending points, while other signed-in players use an atomic, idempotent 25-point server debit per new saved pack. Imports and edits remain free.

releases.title: The timeline slider finds its moment
releases.summary: Dragging the long-timeline navigator now selects the matching card and scrolls it into view consistently in local and multiplayer games.
details: Every range-slider movement updates the selected card immediately instead of waiting for a separate button action or leaving the board behind.
Local and multiplayer boards now share the same card-centering behavior, including smooth scrolling and the Reduce motion preference.
The chosen card keeps a visible selection outline after the brief arrival animation ends, making the slider position easy to confirm.
Horizontal navigation centers within the timeline while using the nearest vertical position, so finding a card no longer pulls the slider unnecessarily out of view.

releases.title: Every message and every turn stays clear
releases.summary: Room chat now keeps notifications readable, sounds for new messages, brings direct mentions forward, labels card values, and holds multiplayer turns steady while a move is being saved.
details: The collapsed room-chat dock now gives its notification indicator, label, status, and sound control enough space to remain readable on narrow phones.

New room messages play a dedicated chat cue, while an exact @room player name automatically opens an in-app alert for that player and can request an away notification; messages hidden by either player's block remain hidden.

Every playable hand card now shows its current value: points in score modes, tiebreak points in Survival, and streak progress in Streak mode, with Hard cards worth two and other difficulties worth one.

Online hands remain locked from the first placement request through any bounded network retry, preventing unrelated loading state and delayed polling from making a turn flash between playable and unavailable.

releases.title: The changelog is always within reach
releases.summary: Quick Play difficulty and desktop release notes now stay accessible from Home and Downloads, with clear loading, offline, and retry states.
details: Manual changelog access now loads the public release history on demand instead of depending on the delayed startup notice request.
The full changelog remains available even when automatic release notices are disabled, so staff notification settings never hide a player-requested history.
Loading, offline, and failed-request states are visible inside the accessible dialog, with a keyboard-friendly retry action.

releases.title: The whole story at the finish
releases.summary: Host setup now has a dependable route back, and every completed game can review and replay its final timeline across desktop and mobile.
details: The Back control inside the first Host setup step now returns to the multiplayer menu instead of appearing disabled; on later steps it continues to move backward through the wizard.
Solo, local, Chronicle challenge, and online result screens now show the full final timeline in chronological order with dates and the player responsible for each placement.
A player-controlled quick time-lapse reveals the final timeline event by event, with pause, continue, replay, and Show all now controls.
The expanded result card remains internally scrollable, stacks controls on narrow screens, and suppresses timeline transitions when Reduce motion is enabled.

releases.title: Every turn arrives intact
releases.summary: Multiplayer turns now resist delayed polls and failed writes, while faster game and chat refreshes keep desktop and mobile tables visibly in sync.
details: Room snapshots now carry a durable revision, and clients reject older asynchronous responses so a late poll cannot replace a newly completed turn.
Routine room polls no longer write the whole room; periodic liveness heartbeats and automatic turn transitions use compare-and-swap so they cannot overwrite a concurrent card placement.

A failed durable card write now rejects and reloads instead of appearing successful and disappearing later, while active room polling, room chat, and direct messages refresh faster without overlapping requests.
Turns no longer use an undocumented ninety-second skip: players advance automatically only when the host explicitly enables a turn timer or disconnected-player skip rule.

releases.title: Hosts can reshape the table
releases.summary: Hosts can now change card packs and every room customization while the lobby is waiting, with the updated setup shared across desktop and mobile before the game begins.
details: The host can reopen Room setup after creating a room and change the selected card packs, visibility, and room rules from one place.
Pack changes are applied to the authoritative room, refresh the card count and deck name for every player, and remain available even after the host marks ready while the room is still waiting.
Once play starts, the server locks all room customization so the active game's deck and rules cannot change underneath the players.

releases.title: Chat takes the clear side
releases.summary: Room chat now docks on the left so the release, audio, and Customize controls stay visible on the right across desktop and mobile, with clean collapse behavior for every floating surface.
details: Collapsed room chat stays in a bounded left-side dock instead of stretching beneath the right-side floating controls.
Open desktop chat reserves left-side board space; on narrow screens, open chat uses the available viewport while the right-side utility dock yields cleanly.
The release badge, audio control, Customize button, chat toggle, and card-detail modal remain independently accessible without covering one another.

releases.title: Chat and details keep their space
releases.summary: Room chat and floating card details now stay out of each other’s way on desktop and mobile, with clearer collapse controls and viewport-safe panels.
details: Opening card details raises the modal above the room chat and temporarily hides lower-priority floating controls so the story stays readable.
Expanded room chat yields the floating Customize dock, while its header clearly announces the collapse action and keeps the chat state easy to restore.
Card details and open chat respect safe areas, keyboard-sized viewports, and narrow widths without clipping their content.

releases.title: Cards make room for the next chapter
releases.summary: Full placement animation now makes the timeline visibly push cards aside before the new card settles into its gap on desktop and mobile, with a device setting to turn the motion off and larger default placement targets.
details: Dragging or choosing a card stages a full push-and-insert animation across local and online timelines before the existing authoritative placement is submitted.
Full placement animation is on by default, saved with accessibility preferences, and automatically yields to Reduce motion.
Timeline placement areas are a little wider on desktop and mobile and taller in vertical layouts, making gaps easier to hit.

releases.title: A name that follows you into chat
releases.summary: Chat now uses the player name everywhere, lets players change it from the chat surface, and keeps the desktop release aligned while asking unnamed players for one before sending.
details: Social chat and room chat now show an editable player name so messages use the same identity as the rest of Time Chronicles.
Opening room chat reconciles the durable player profile with the name used at that table before chat messages load.
Players without a name see a focused name setup panel when chat opens, and the composer stays locked until a name is saved.

releases.title: A friendlier table on every phone
releases.summary: Room setup now keeps each difficulty and mode choice close to its explanation, advanced rules stay out of the way until needed, and mobile chat opens into a keyboard-safe composer without the utility controls covering it.
details: Mobile room-rule cards no longer inherit a tall desktop flex basis, so labels, explanations, and controls stay together with comfortable spacing.
Core choices remain immediately visible while hand, reconnect, visibility, chat, and card-detail options move into a clearly labeled Advanced room rules section.
The mobile utility dock becomes one compact row with icon-sized audio and Customize controls, leaving more of the game and setup visible.
Room chat now focuses its text composer from the mobile chat action, follows visual-viewport keyboard changes, keeps 16-pixel input text to prevent browser zoom, and supports Enter to send.
Failed messages preserve their retry action without permanently disabling the composer, and the utility dock clears the screen while a player is typing.

releases.title: A safer way to talk at the table
releases.summary: Moderated room chat, same-age-band friends and direct messages, and a private 13+ social gate bring conversation to online games without adding a paid chat provider, while Challenge Chronicle difficulty stays aligned at every width.
details: Public, invite-only, and private online rooms now include filtered text chat with quick phrases, message retry states, blocking, reporting, deletion, and host channel controls.
The Social hub adds opaque friend codes, requests, friends, same-age-band direct messages, unread counts, blocking, safety guidance, and social-data deletion without public user search.
Birth month and year are evaluated on the server and discarded; under-13 players can keep playing while chat, friends, and direct messages remain unavailable.
Room messages expire after 7 days, direct messages after 30 days, and redacted moderation snapshots after 90 days, with durable rate limits and bounded channel history.
Staff moderation adds reviewed cases, message deletion, player warnings, timed or permanent social suspensions, audit entries, recent-MFA enforcement, and an immediate Social Chat kill switch.
Challenge Chronicle's difficulty row now stays aligned inside its panel and stacks cleanly at tablet, mobile, and enlarged-text widths.

releases.title: Every pack has a place
releases.summary: Challenge Chronicle makes deck choice visible up front, keeps locked packs discoverable, and gives every pack a clear path to preview or unlock while Quick Play and the desktop release stay aligned.
details: Challenge Chronicle now shows the full active pack catalog before Advanced rules & setup, so choosing a deck is part of the main setup flow.
Locked packs stay visible in the scrollable deck picker with All packs, Unlocked, and Locked filters; locked cards cannot be selected until they are unlocked.
Each locked pack promotes its theme, offers a date-safe preview, and links directly to a points unlock when ready or the full Deck Builder unlock path.
The narrow Customize panel now fills its available viewport cleanly, keeping theme controls and the internal scroll area usable on small screens.
The signed desktop web bundle and release identity are updated to 0.9.141.

releases.title: Difficulty that travels with the table
releases.summary: Five difficulty levels now shape every game, Quick Play chapters can move easier or harder, and desktop updates open a complete installer catalog in the system browser.
details: Casual, Easy, Normal, Hard, and Expert use explicit card mixes, Quick Play mistake allowances, and Chronicle placement accuracy across solo, AI, Local, Nearby, and Online play.
Casual misses and timeouts reveal and correctly insert the card with no points, heart, streak, draw, source-opening, or solo-ending penalty.
Every five-correct-card Quick Play chapter offers Easier, Keep level, and Harder choices while retaining total run statistics and resetting that chapter's mistake allowance.
Native update and download actions now open the operating system browser; no installer is embedded or run inside the game.
The in-app and public Downloads pages show Windows NSIS, universal macOS DMG, and Linux AppImage, DEB, and RPM installers with sizes, SHA-256 checksums, requirements, instructions, and release notes.

releases.title: Three new eras and a better Deck Builder
releases.summary: Music, pandemic-scale outbreaks, and animal history join the catalog as unlockable 50-card packs, while duplicate events are replaced and deck building becomes a searchable customization workspace.
details: Music of the Ages, Viral Outbreaks, and Animals through the Ages each add 50 sourced timeline events and can be unlocked with earned points.
The full 1,050-card collection now uses unique event titles and source-year combinations, replacing duplicate or effectively repeated events across packs without breaking saved deck identifiers.
Deck Builder brings owned and locked packs into one searchable workspace with scope filters, sorting, unlock readiness, previews, and one-click custom copies of owned packs.
Authorized staff can securely give, remove, or reset player points and grant or revoke packs as staff awards or promotions, with MFA, CSRF protection, idempotency, and audit logging.

releases.title: A table that fits your screen
releases.summary: Responsive desktop, tablet, and mobile room browsing stays inside its panel, the floating Customize dock gains a fuller mixer and role-based palettes, and every live board can flip between horizontal and vertical timelines.
details: Room search and filters now reflow on desktop, tablet, and mobile without clipping the last control beyond the panel edge.
The floating Audio panel adds a master output slider while keeping independent music and sound-effects controls, previews, and track selection.
Color palettes now expose primary, secondary, highlight, success, and danger roles with device-local custom colors.
A small board control switches local and online timelines between horizontal and vertical layouts during a game; the choice remains local to each player.

releases.title: Desktop downloads, updates, and latest-only installer storage
releases.summary: Desktop builds ship native signed updates alongside the latest platform installers; older installers are retired on every publication to keep storage minimal.
details: The desktop app Download button now checks for signed native updates instead of showing the web installer catalog.

Every release publishes the latest Windows, macOS, and Linux installers; the previous version's installers and updater manifests are retired, so the public download catalog always holds exactly one release.
The native updater prompt guides players through downloading, installing, and restarting the signed desktop update inside the app.
Web app visitors continue to see the full download catalog with platform-specific installers, SHA-256 checksums, and the PWA fallback.

releases.title: Results stay until you close them
releases.summary: Placement and final results stay on screen until the player clicks to close them, instead of auto-dismissing while a multiplayer table waits for the next input.
details: Play announcements no longer vanish after six seconds. Close or inspect them when you are ready.
Refreshing a room no longer clears an open placement result, and a finished table keeps its results overlay even if someone else returns the room to the lobby.
Timed-out turns open a result you can read, and the winner screen has an explicit Close results control plus a Show results button to bring it back.

releases.title: Game modes and first-run How to Play
releases.summary: Survival and Time Attack keep their own stakes instead of converting back to a Classic points race, and first-time or inactive players get a blocking tutorial How to Play button they can dismiss.
details: Survival still ends on hearts, even with a turn clock, and Time Attack keeps racing the timer to the target score instead of ending a solo run on the first miss like Classic.
A first-time or inactive welcome sits on top of Home with a real How to Play button, a Not now dismiss, Escape, and a tap outside the card.
Local setup can add an optional turn clock to any mode, including Survival, without changing the selected win condition.

releases.title: Multiplayer unstick and moderation close
releases.summary: Online rooms recover from stuck turns, and deleting a table from staff immediately tells seated players it was closed by moderation.
details: Staff room delete and clear-all write a durable close record so other instances cannot resurrect the table, and seated players hear a calm close and leave with a moderation message.
A silent active seat is skipped after 90 seconds so classic, survival, time-attack, streak, and blitz games keep moving even when the host turn timer is off.
Refreshing mid-game returns players to the live table instead of trapping them on a reconnect lobby, and closed rooms clear the saved session instead of retrying forever.

releases.title: Hosted PayPal donate
releases.summary: The Store and home footer now use the live PayPal Donate button so players can support Time Chronicles while paid unlocks wait on the seller transition.
details: The Store donation panel posts to PayPal's hosted Donate checkout with button R6225SLR29F3G instead of a disabled server checkout.
The home footer includes a Donate button that opens the same PayPal hosted form.
Pack unlocks stay earn-first; hosted donations do not grant client-only entitlements.

releases.title: Donation-only current unlocks
releases.summary: Before 1.0, the store hides unavailable subscription tiers and verified PayPal support donations can unlock the current catalog together with ad-free play.
details: The public Store and Support screens hide unavailable monthly, yearly, lifetime, and Stripe pack purchase controls, and locked packs point at verified PayPal donations instead of an unable-to-purchase state.

A verified donation now records durable access to all current packs and the selected tier of temporary ad-free play, while the server still validates the PayPal amount, capture, webhook, and recovery code.
The temporary donation-only mode defaults on and can be switched off later with CHRONICLE_PAYPAL_DONATION_ONLY=0 when the seller account transition is complete.

releases.title: PayPal unlock readiness
releases.summary: PayPal support checkout now gates server-verified donations, subscriptions, lifetime access, and pack purchases behind complete provider configuration.
details: PayPal Orders and Subscriptions use server-created metadata, provider amount checks, capture verification, and durable recovery codes.
Signed PayPal webhooks update recurring subscription state and recover one-time purchases when a browser return is interrupted.
PayPal actions stay hidden until protected credentials, a webhook ID, and the explicit unlock flag are configured; Stripe remains a separate future provider.

releases.title: Drop stale turn notifications
releases.summary: A gone turn notification endpoint is removed from the room immediately instead of being retried until it expires.
details: Web Push 404 and 410 responses are treated as gone rather than a successful wake-up.
The room drops that subscription as soon as the next-player notification reports it gone.

releases.title: Profile-bound game telemetry
releases.summary: Game summary telemetry now requires a player profile, while anonymous visits keep a tighter support-safe IP limit.
details: Anonymous player.visit events remain allowed with a reduced per-IP rate limit.
game.summary events require a player-profile bearer and are capped per profile and IP per day.

releases.title: Live settings fail-closed
releases.summary: A Mongo outage now keeps the last live room settings, or pauses room creation, instead of reopening the table.
details: Failed staff live-config reads no longer reset economy and weekly poll costs to defaults.
Public live-ops returns the last good payload, or HTTP 503 with maintenance on when none exists.

releases.title: Unexpected API errors as 500
releases.summary: Unexpected multiplayer and billing failures now return HTTP 500 instead of looking like a client request error.
details: Known room, auth, and validation messages still return 400, 401, or 404.
Untagged internal failures no longer default to HTTP 400.

releases.title: Public write rate limits
releases.summary: Profile, weekly poll, and push writes now share the same public rate and body limits as support requests.
details: Production and local servers cap weekly poll POST bodies and rate-limit profile, poll, and push writes.
Repeated public writes return HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header.

releases.title: Retry transient missing rooms
releases.summary: Room polls retry a brief Room not found miss so a cold multiplayer instance does not drop the table.
details: Client restore, reconnect, and refresh paths retry missing rooms; expired rooms still fail immediately.
The server force-refreshes durable storage and reads the room key before answering 404.

releases.title: Production storage fail-closed
releases.summary: Vercel now refuses silent in-memory rooms and profiles when durable storage is missing.
details: Production requires blob storage for rooms, polls, and tickets, and MongoDB for player profiles.
Health reports rooms as unavailable instead of claiming a durable store when Vercel is misconfigured.

releases.title: Weekly poll storage fail-closed
releases.summary: A room storage outage no longer overwrites the weekly community poll with an empty board.
details: Failed weekly poll reads keep the last in-memory cycle or return unavailable.
Missing poll storage still seeds the first cycle; read failures never persist an empty cycle.

releases.title: No charge for rejected pack ideas
releases.summary: Weekly pack requests now validate the idea first, so a duplicate or invalid title does not spend room points.
details: Idea title, category, and duplicate checks run before points are spent.
Only an accepted weekly idea charges the player profile.

releases.title: One vote per player profile
releases.summary: Weekly poll submissions and votes now follow a signed-in player profile instead of a browser-chosen participant name that could be changed to vote again.
details: Submitting or voting on the weekly poll requires a player profile, and limits are keyed to that profile.
Anonymous browser participant ids remain only for unsigned-in poll viewing.

releases.title: Proven push subscriptions
releases.summary: Turn notifications now require a seat token and only accept public Web Push hosts, so a public player id cannot attach a hostile endpoint.
details: Push subscribe requires the room reconnect token and binds the device to that seated player.
Subscription endpoints must be HTTPS Web Push hosts; private, local, and metadata addresses are rejected.

releases.title: Safer online room updates
releases.summary: Online rooms now keep concurrent joins, host changes, and moves instead of letting one serverless write erase another.
details: Each room stores a write revision and durable updates use compare-and-swap, so overlapping joins and host transfers retry instead of dropping a player.
A stale instance can no longer overwrite a newer room snapshot during a poll or persist.

releases.title: A wider table and verified PayPal unlocks
releases.summary: Desktop multiplayer now uses the available width, while PayPal can mirror the catalog with server-verified donations, packs, lifetime access, and subscriptions.
details: Reworked the desktop multiplayer entry screen into a readable intro and room-control composition that collapses to one column on compact screens.
Added PayPal Orders and Subscriptions checkout with server-calculated sale pricing, protected credentials, capture verification, durable recovery codes, and webhook lifecycle handling.
PayPal catalog unlocks now mirror the same product benefits, compare-at prices, promotions, and future-pack choices as the server catalog; client-only donation claims are no longer trusted.
Release automation now publishes the latest signed Windows, Linux, and macOS installers while pruning older public installers and updater manifests.

releases.title: Support tickets and a stronger table handoff
releases.summary: Players can follow support tickets in-app while staff can assign, resolve, reply to, soft-delete, and restore them; saved rooms and host handoffs are clearer too.
details: Replaced the Support Inbox with a permission-scoped Support tickets workflow for status, priority, assignment, private notes, staff replies, acknowledgement requests, close/reopen, soft-delete, restore, and audit history.
Players now keep the original request in a ticket conversation, receive in-app follow-up notices, and can acknowledge or send requested details after reconnecting.
Added a dedicated Social staff role and permission-scoped social content calendar with drafts, review states, schedules, links, and audited changes.
Staff invitations now make the username optional by deriving a sensible starting name from the invite email.
The saved-room popup now lets a non-host leave or a host disband the room instead of forcing an unnecessary reconnect.
When a host leaves or is removed, the room selects the next eligible player and tells that player they are now the host.

releases.title: A clearer mobile home
releases.summary: Mobile home navigation now uses the first screen more efficiently, keeping the main play choices visible through Store.
details: Removed the extra top spacing from the mobile home layout.
Tightened mobile menu rhythm and button sizing so Quick Play through Store fit in the first viewport without hiding the first-player prompt.

releases.title: Clearer support and updates
releases.summary: Pricing can now be managed from staff controls, returning players get a clear menu action, and update notifications respect player activity.
details: Monthly support starts at $4.99, annual support is $47.90, and each future pack is $0.99; live promotions show sale pricing, compare-at prices, copy, and end dates.
PayPal support is clearly described as helping the developer and providing an ad-free thank-you without unlocking card packs.
The saved Chronicle Run prompt now uses a button-style Return to menu action, and New to the Timeline appears before Quick Play for a clearer first decision.
Staff can turn live notifications on or off and choose whether startup release notes target first-time or inactive players, all players, or nobody.

releases.title: Tap or drag
releases.summary: The tutorial now labels both gestures beside the pointer and lets every player tap, click, or drag the sample card.
details: The pointer cue now says Tap/Drag right beside the hand or cursor, making the available actions clear at a glance.
Tap or click still selects the sample card and the glowing gap completes the move.
A pointer drag is now available on touch and desktop devices, so the sample card can be picked up and carried into the gap directly.

releases.title: Point, then place
releases.summary: The tutorial now points directly at the card to move and lets desktop players drag it through a real pointer gesture into the glowing gap.
details: The hand cue now sits above the highlighted card and points down at the one card a new player should move.
Desktop drag is a real pointer drag: the card follows the pointer, the destination gap highlights on contact, and a check mark confirms the placement.
Tap and click placement keep the same friendly check-mark result, so every input path teaches the same move.

releases.title: See the move
releases.summary: How to play now looks like a real timeline with three cards, one clear card to move, and a gentle path to its glowing gap.
details: The tutorial board starts with three dated cards already in order, so new players can see what a timeline looks like before making a move.
One child-friendly card is highlighted as the card to move, while the destination gap glows and a soft animated pointer shows the path.
Touch players see a tap cue; desktop players see a drag cue. Both interactions can be practiced directly in the tutorial.

releases.title: A clearer way in
releases.summary: Home navigation now groups multiplayer, Deck Builder, Store, and Stats together, while How to play becomes a short interactive drag-or-tap lesson.
details: The main menu keeps Multiplayer followed by Deck Builder, Stats, and Store, so the tools for building and exploring a table stay together.
The extra home menu is now labeled More ways to play, help & settings and keeps advanced play, settings, updates, support, and How to play in one clear group.
How to play is a single interactive card-and-gap screen: desktop shows a cursor and click-drag instruction, while mobile shows a tap cue and tap-the-card-then-gap instruction.
The tutorial demo accepts the same click, drag, or tap gesture it explains before the player starts a real game.

releases.title: Name your table
releases.summary: Returning players now see the readable room name first, including for invite-only tables, instead of having to recognize an invite code.
details: The saved-room prompt identifies the table by its room name and keeps the invite code as a small confirmation detail.
Existing saved sessions from earlier releases resolve their room name on return, so invite-only games become understandable without changing how players reconnect.
New and refreshed multiplayer sessions save the room name locally for an immediate, readable prompt on the next app launch.

releases.title: Back to the table
releases.summary: The classic timeline and playable board return as the defaults, while timeline direction and board presentation remain configurable in Settings.
details: Classic play now starts with the familiar side-by-side scores, board, timeline, and hand instead of a compressed or displaced game surface.
Choose a horizontal or vertical timeline and a classic or focused play area in Settings; choices stay saved locally without changing the game rules.
Correct and missed cards keep their turn-by-turn result messages, revealed card details, and clear next action in Solo, Local, and multiplayer play.
Timeline navigation stays available for longer stories without crowding the opening moves, and placement feedback remains actionable without covering the board.
Responsive sizing keeps the timeline, hand, result actions, and controls reachable on desktop, tablet, and phone layouts.

releases.title: Your timeline, your direction
releases.summary: Horizontal scrolling returns as the default, with a vertical option, faster long-timeline navigation, and clearer placement reviews.
details: Choose a horizontal or vertical timeline in Settings or Customize. The preference stays on this device and works in local and multiplayer games.
Jump to the start, latest card, or any exact card position on a long timeline. Selecting a placement notification highlights the card you want to find.
Correct placements jump to their card; missed and timed-out cards open the revealed card details so every turn remains useful.
The first-play preview now shows a card moving into place, while Quick Play remains the clear skip-to-game path beside the optional tutorial.
Reduced-motion settings replace the placement animation with a still explanation.

releases.title: A faster first play and a deeper chronicle
releases.summary: Quick Play now starts the game immediately, with a readable solo board, clearer placement feedback, and a persistent five-chapter Chronicle Run.
details: Quick Play is the first action: no setup form, release modal, tutorial tour, music prompt, or optional network request blocks the first card.
The first move is taught inside the timeline with an accessible animated guide, while advanced modes, collections, settings, and the full tutorial remain available from More.
Solo play uses a full-width vertical timeline, compact Chronicle Run progress, inline placement results, and a final review that keeps the actual timeline and last move visible.
Chronicle Run chapters carry mistakes and optional risk modifiers forward, save the best progress locally, and increase the difficulty mix without erasing progress after a failed run.
Quick Play mixes science, culture, games, music, film, sports, food, weather, and other everyday moments, with sourced cards and stronger default readability.

releases.title: Multiplayer identity, turn integrity, and live status fixes
releases.summary: Online rooms no longer duplicate a player when the same device re-enters, turns can no longer skip or roll back across serverless instances, and the board now shows every player's connection state with the active player's remaining time.
details: Device-based seats: each browser gets a stable device id, and re-joining a room (or recovering after a lost session) reclaims that device's original seat instead of adding a duplicate player — same seat, same hand, fresh reconnect token.

Turn integrity: polls now re-read the newest durable room state before acting, so a recycled serverless instance can no longer resolve a turn it had already advanced (skipping players) or write an older snapshot back that rolls the board to a previous turn.
The client ignores stale poll snapshots entirely, so a momentary cross-instance lag can never roll the timeline backward on screen.

The scoreboard marks each player online or away next to their name and shows the active player's countdown (e.g. "online · 12s left"), so a dropped or lagging connection is visible instead of silently stalling the table.

releases.title: Store sales engine, cleaner ads, and clearer lobby messaging
releases.summary: The store can now run time-boxed sales with percent-off or fixed prices and bonus incentives, the ad slot cleans up stray Google iframes when it unmounts, and the Online lobby explains why an empty room list can be misleading.
details: A shared billing sales model validates staff-configured sales (percent-off or fixed price, active window, bonus days or bonus points) and exposes discounted price helpers with compare-at pricing.
Staff global settings and the public live-ops payload now carry the billing configuration and an optional active sale for the store.
Unmounting an ad slot removes leftover Google ad iframes that could linger on screen after navigating away.
The Online lobby's empty state now notes that a table only shows while someone is actually waiting in it, so players are not confused by a quiet room list.

releases.title: Lobby, dock, and ad hit-target fixes
releases.summary: The Online lobby badge no longer crowds the room title, the floating customize and mute controls stop blocking the screen, and the bottom ad is clickable again.
details: The "Room waiting" badge is spaced off the room title so the two never overlap.
The floating dock (customize and mute) now ignores clicks on its empty strip area, so it no longer sits in the way of the content behind it.
The ad's label and frame no longer swallow clicks: GO AD-FREE, the ad itself, and its close button all respond again.

releases.title: Online lobby hotfix
releases.summary: The public Online lobby no longer comes up empty on the serverless deployment: rooms created on one instance now appear in the lobby on every instance, so players can find and join each other again. Joining by room code continues to work across instances.
details: Rooms are no longer marked fully disconnected when a fresh serverless instance reloads them from durable storage; a player who polled recently still counts as present.
The public lobby now lists waiting rooms hosted on any serverless instance, instead of hiding every room the local instance had not seen yet.
Joining by invite code resolves rooms across instances exactly as before, and ghost rooms whose owners stopped polling are still swept.

releases.title: Online room creation hotfix
releases.summary: Creating or joining an online room no longer crashes when the serverless request has no socket. Vercel forwarded headers are used instead, so hosting works again on mobile and desktop.
details: Room create, join, and reconnect no longer throw when request.socket is null on Vercel.
Client IP and location still come from x-forwarded-for and Vercel geo headers for moderation and analytics.

releases.title: Fairer prices, quieter ads, and staff live ops
releases.summary: Empty AdSense panels stay hidden until a real ad fills. The store now uses a $4.99 monthly, $39.99 yearly, and $19.99 lifetime ladder, with PayPal as an ad-free thank-you rather than a pack unlock. Reward cadence is staff-owned, double-points events pop up when they go live, and a new Polls tool records player answers.
details: AdSense chrome collapses unless a filled ad is present, so loading and unfilled states no longer leave a cream gap; the Monydragon sponsor still appears as the fallback.
Store prices realign around $4.99/month, a new $39.99/year plan, $19.99 lifetime, and $0.99 future packs. PayPal thank-you tiers match that monthly rung and grant ad-free time only.
Players no longer pick a reward cadence. Staff set cards-per-point (default 1 point every 10 cards) and can schedule point-multiplier events that pop up when they activate.
A new staff Polls & questions tool lets the team compose surveys, collect one response per player, and mark results Reviewed, Acted on, or Closed.

releases.title: Deck Builder, feedback, and a fuller history
releases.summary: The Deck Builder becomes the paid creative suite: players browse and manage decks free, while making new custom cards or decks unlocks through the $2.99/month subscription, the $9.99 lifetime unlock, or earned points. Support now accepts problem reports and feature suggestions in-app, Customize warns when colors become hard to read, room cleanup is fixed, and the changelog restores the complete pre-0.9.58 history in expandable sections.
details: The home menu no longer advertises Projects; the Deck Builder is the creative home. Managing existing custom decks and building a collection from unlocked cards stays free, while creating a brand-new deck or card requires the subscription, the lifetime unlock, or enough earned points.
A clear paywall explains the three unlock paths ($2.99/month, $9.99 once, or points) directly in the Deck Builder instead of sending players to a hidden studio.
Community feedback now offers Report a problem and Suggest a feature beside the existing card-correction flow, so every report lands in the staff inbox and routes to support@monydragon.com.
Customize warns in real time when custom text, background, or accent colors fall below readable contrast in light, dark, or system mode, so ambiguous combinations never go unnoticed.

The changelog is now expandable per release — only the latest version opens automatically, and every earlier version collapses into its own section — with the full release history before 0.9.58 restored.
Automatic room pruning now removes ghost, empty, and expired rooms during every durable-store refresh, and staff can clear every room with one confirmed action.

releases.title: Signed desktop updates and live table tools
releases.summary: Installed Windows, Linux, and macOS apps can now check for a signed update, confirm, install, and relaunch. Stats is split into Achievements, Offline, and Online. Home and Store show a live weekly countdown, staff can price packs and votes, rooms put the table name first, and anyone at the table can suggest or offer owned packs. Staff gains a Moderation console with IP, location, and identity tools plus a player-matching Customize dock.
details: Desktop builds check the signed updater feed, show a confirmation prompt, and can install then relaunch. Manual downloads remain available if an update is skipped.
Stats now uses three page tabs: Achievements, Stats (Offline) combining Solo and Local, and Stats (Online).
Home and Store show a live countdown to weekly poll close and the next pack release, including staff-configured request and vote point costs.
Online profiles bootstrap on first use, migrate local progress once, and treat the server wallet and entitlements as authoritative while connected.
Lobby packs are room-only: anyone can suggest, and a pack is in the game only while at least one seated owner offers it. Room name is the in-play heading, with the code as secondary metadata.
Staff Moderation shows IP, coarse location, and name fallbacks, hosts allow/deny lists and kick/delete controls, Pack studio can grant a pack, and Customize matches the player Theme/Settings dock.

releases.title: Clear multiplayer paths and readable rooms everywhere
releases.summary: Multiplayer now starts with Host, Join by Room, or Join by Invite Code, public rooms can be searched, filtered, and sorted, and host setup stays bounded on every screen. Dark-mode staff dialogs and shared surfaces are readable, community-voted packs show their release date, and empty ad banners no longer leave a white gap.
details: Multiplayer opens with three direct choices: Host, Join by Room, and Join by Invite Code. Hosting then offers Local, Nearby (Coming soon), and Online without sending players through unrelated screens.

The public Online lobby now supports search, deck, seat, and status filters plus recent-activity, open-seat, and name sorting. Room cards join directly, while Invite Code and Online Lobby actions stay one tap away.
Room timer and disconnect controls shrink and stack inside their settings cards instead of extending beyond the border at narrower desktop and tablet widths.
Staff forms, cards, previews, and the sensitive-action verification dialog use theme-aware surfaces and readable text in dark mode; shared accent panels now use dark-safe tones too.
Weekly community winners no longer carry a Community: name prefix. Deck details identify them as community-voted packs and show the actual release date.
Unfilled AdSense placements collapse instead of reserving an empty white strip, and first-party fallback banners match the active theme.

releases.title: A friendlier multiplayer lobby and mobile inputs that work
releases.summary: The online lobby is now organized into tabs — Host, Join Room, and Join with code — with a guided host setup, so nobody scrolls a wall of host-only controls. Joining without a name asks first, numeric inputs edit properly on phones, and hung connections time out instead of freezing the table.
details: The online lobby is split into three tabs: Host a room (a guided Table, Cards, Rules, Launch setup), Join room (browse public tables with search and filters), and Join with code (direct invite), so the action you want is always in reach on mobile and desktop.
Joining a room without a player name now pops a name prompt with the room code shown; the join stays disabled until a name is entered, then proceeds straight into the room.

Numeric pickers and custom amounts are editable on iOS: the number inputs use a numeric keypad text field instead of the iOS number input that could not be cleared or changed, and the Custom amount option can be re-selected after typing.
Online requests now time out after a hard ceiling, so a hung connection is reported and retried instead of leaving the room poll stuck on a stale turn.
The host setup, room list, and invite join all fit comfortably on phones and desktops with tabbed sections instead of one long scrolling form.

releases.title: Unstick frozen turns and put Customize everywhere
releases.summary: A stuck online turn now recovers with one tap: the game screen gains a Refresh room control that pulls the authoritative server state, and a rejected placement automatically resyncs instead of freezing the table. The floating Customize button is now a first-class control on by default, opening a tabbed popup with Theme, Audio, and Settings from any screen — so switching the music is one tap away.
details: The multiplayer game screen adds a Refresh room button that force-pulls the latest room snapshot, clears stuck busy/move flags and stale selections, and shows a Room synced confirmation under the turn status.
When the server rejects a placement because the turn, hand, or game already changed, the client now resyncs immediately so a ghost 'Your turn' can never block every player at the table.
The floating Customize button is on by default for everyone, including returning players whose saved preferences still carried the old off default — their other choices are preserved.

Customize now opens a popup with tabs at the top: Theme keeps the full appearance panel, Audio embeds the complete mixer with music, effects, volumes, and previews, and Settings holds the reading & access toggles plus a jump to the full Settings screen.
Music is easier than ever to update: mute, volumes, and the track picker live in the Audio tab of the floating dock on the home screen, in a game, or anywhere else in the app.

releases.title: Rejoin your last room, and pushes that survive restarts
releases.summary: Opening the app after a close now asks whether you want to rejoin your last room — one tap reconnects instantly and drops you back onto the shared timeline. Turn pushes are stored with the room itself, so a closed or hibernated app still wakes when the turn reaches you, even after a server restart.
details: A popup on app entry offers to rejoin your last room — one tap drops you straight back onto the shared timeline.
Turn pushes now survive server restarts: your device subscription is stored with the room, so a closed or hibernated app still wakes when it's your turn.
Closed-app push wake-ups land on the rejoin prompt, so returning from a notification goes straight to your room.

releases.title: Cleaner end screens and a sturdier desktop bundle
releases.summary: The winner screen keeps every piece of text and every control on its own line with proper spacing, and the desktop app now boots from a single bundled script so the native shell cannot blank out while loading the game.
details: The winner and result popups get explicit breathing room: the Play again button, the players list, the return note, and the Leave room link can no longer crowd or overlap one another on phones, tablets, or desktops.
Long winner names wrap instead of colliding with the scores, and narrow screens keep every end-screen row visible inside the viewport.
The desktop application now embeds the whole game in one static bundle — no dynamic chunks to resolve over Tauri's custom protocol — so the window paints the game instead of a blank white screen.
The installed app keeps its local decks, audio, settings, and offline play; the same bundle still powers the Swift and web builds.

releases.title: A clearer clock and a tidier board
releases.summary: Time Attack shows a large, glanceable countdown with a configurable per-turn limit, timeline dates no longer clip off the edges of cards, the Settings & customize button sits flush on the home menu, and the Solo/Pass & play hint is gone.
details: Time Attack now displays a prominent countdown above the board that pulses red in the final five seconds, in both local and online games.
The per-turn timer stays configurable from setup and room settings, and every mode was re-verified end to end across local and multiplayer tables.
Card dates wrap cleanly and the mobile timeline cards grow to fit longer full dates instead of clipping them at the bottom edge.
The Settings & customize button spans the full home utility row so its label and gear icon stay aligned on one line.
The home-screen "Solo runs in Single Player · Pass & play in Multiplayer" hint and its avatar icons have been removed.

releases.title: Turns reach you even in the background
releases.summary: Online rooms now deliver a real Web Push notification when the shared turn reaches you, so a minimized or suspended phone still wakes with your turn and taps straight back onto the timeline.
details: While a game is live, the app subscribes the device to background turn pushes and registers it against your online seat; leaving the room drops the registration.
The server sends a VAPID-signed wake-up to the newly active player on every turn advance, including moves, timeouts, away skips, and departures.
The installed service worker shows the turn notification even when the app is closed or backgrounded, and tapping it focuses the app and jumps back onto the shared timeline.
Push only activates when the player has already granted notification permission, and platforms without push support skip it silently.

releases.title: Tap the alert and land back on the timeline
releases.summary: Tapping a turn or game-complete notification now brings the app forward, reopens the active table, and scrolls straight to the timeline so a player is one tap from their next move.
details: The strong turn pulse still fires while the app is minimized or backgrounded, and tapping the notification now deep-links back into the live game instead of just refocusing the tab.
Local, solo, pass-and-play, and online rooms each restore their own board; a player who wandered back to Home is returned to the game in progress.
Returning players land on the shared timeline, scrolled into view on phones and desktops, so the next card is already in front of them.

releases.title: See where each card lands
releases.summary: After a correct placement the result popup now offers “See where it landed”: it closes the popup, scrolls the board to the card's new spot, highlights it, and opens the card's full story and source.
details: The result popup gains a See where it landed action on correct placements in local, pass-and-play, versus, and online rooms.
The board smooth-scrolls to the exact card, pulses a highlight around it, then opens the card's info panel with its full story and source.
Misses and timeouts keep the existing flow, since the card returns to the archive rather than joining the timeline.

releases.title: Joining a room skips the host-only scroll
releases.summary: Room setup controls are now collapsible in the multiplayer lobby: expanded for the host and collapsed by default for guests, so a joiner reaches the player list and Ready button without scrolling past rules they cannot change.
details: The host sees room setup expanded and can collapse it; guests get it collapsed with a one-line summary of the deck and mode.
The Ready button and player list now sit right after the room code when joining, instead of below a wall of host-only settings.
The toggle is keyboard-focusable and exposes aria-expanded/aria-controls for assistive tech.

releases.title: Desktop apps open on the game, not a white window
releases.summary: The Windows desktop installer now opens the full embedded game instead of a blank white window. The native bundle's asset paths are locked to the relative form Tauri's shell requires, and CI rebuilds and verifies that bundle on each build runner before the installer is packaged.
details: Fixed the white screen: native builds could lose the desktop build flag in CI and embed absolute /assets/ URLs, which Tauri's custom protocol serves from the wrong origin and leaves an empty window.
Desktop detection now also reads TAURI_ENV_PLATFORM, which tauri-cli always injects into the pre-build step, so the relative ./assets/ paths can no longer regress on CI runners.
Every build runner now rebuilds the desktop web bundle and runs the bundle verifier before tauri build, so a broken or incomplete payload fails fast instead of shipping a blank installer.
The full game remains embedded: all modes, decks, and cards are verified present in the bundled scripts before the native matrix starts.

releases.title: Never miss your turn
releases.summary: The game now sticks by your side: a system notification and flashing tab reach you when a turn or game changes while the app is minimized or in another tab, and phones pulse strongly at the moment the table hands off to you.
details: Turn alerts can fire a system notification and flash the tab title whenever your turn starts or a game finishes while the app is minimized, tabbed out, or backgrounded on a phone.

Local pass-and-play tables pulse the device the moment the handoff reaches the next player, Versus Chronicle buzzes on your human turns, and Online rooms alert you the instant the shared turn becomes yours.
A strong turn pulse (a deliberate double-pulse pattern) runs on phones without opening the app; where vibration is unsupported it is skipped silently.
Alerts and vibration only fire for the player whose turn it is — never during someone else's play, never during a solo run's automated rival, and never while you are looking at the table.
A new Alerts & attention section in Settings lets every player turn each behavior on or off independently and save it on this device, with honest permission and support status.
System notifications ask once through the browser's own permission prompt when the player enables turn alerts, and blocked or unsupported shells gracefully fall back to the flashing tab title.

releases.title: Repackage and verify the desktop installers
releases.summary: A freshly rebuilt Windows, macOS, and Linux installer set ships with every desktop build now verified before release: the complete game bundle is checked for relative paths, embedded content, and healthy installer sizes.
details: Windows, macOS, and Linux installers are rebuilt fresh for this release, and each native bundle now embeds the complete game — the bundled app, all 900 built-in cards, every screen, and all modes — instead of an empty shell.

Every desktop release build verifies the installer payload before shipping: the embedded web bundle is checked for relative asset paths (the cause of the blank white window), all referenced files, and the presence of expected game content.
Each platform installer is also checked against a minimum size floor before publication, so a broken build that packaged an empty app can no longer be published as a real installer.
The staff-only card-source audit artifact no longer ships inside the app or website; it stays out of every bundle while remaining available as a QA deliverable.
Desktop downloads continue to keep only the newest published installer per platform, retiring older versions when a newer release publishes.
The release feed and download page show the exact version, size, and SHA-256 checksum for the single current installer set, and the installable web app remains the lightweight fallback.

releases.title: Ship one current desktop build
releases.summary: Desktop downloads keep only the newest published installer, and the current release ships a fresh native build that opens into the game instead of a white window.
details: The desktop download catalog now stores only the latest published installer per platform; every older version is retired when a newer release publishes, so players always see one current build.
A freshly built Windows, macOS, and Linux desktop installer is published for this release, replacing the outdated build that could open into a blank white window.
Native desktop builds keep loading their bundled assets through relative paths, so the game screen, setup, and every local table render in color instead of a white window.
The desktop release feed and download page continue to show the exact version, size, and SHA-256 checksum for the single current installer set.
The installable web app remains the lightweight fallback and still updates in the browser between desktop releases.

releases.title: Set the soundtrack
releases.summary: The generated music now plays across Home and every screen, fresh players start muted, and a one-time prompt lets new players choose their soundtrack.
details: The original generated soundtrack plays on the Home screen and everywhere else, not just during a game, so the same selected loop follows the player through setup, browsing, and play.
New players start muted by default: nothing plays until they explicitly turn sound on, keeping first launches quiet and deliberate.
A first-run prompt asks new players whether they want music, offers to turn on the default loop, lets them jump straight to choosing a track in Settings, or keeps audio off.
The prompt appears once, after the quick tutorial and release notes, and never interrupts an active game; answering it remembers the choice on this device.
Returning players with saved audio preferences are never re-prompted and keep their existing volume, track, and mute choices.
The always-available Mute dock control and the full Settings mixer continue to work exactly as before.

releases.title: Keep every mode honest
releases.summary: Survival stays heart-driven to the final card, Single Player and Multiplayer keep their own tables, and native desktop installers finally open in color instead of a blank window.
details: Survival mode is decided by hearts alone: a dry archive recycles instead of silently turning into a points race, and the final screen crowns the player with the most hearts left — never the top scorer.
The same heart-driven endgame applies to Solo, Chronicle, Local, Nearby, and Online survival tables through the shared client and server engines.

Single Player setup now offers only Solo runs and the Chronicle challenge; Pass & play appears only in the Multiplayer section, and the home screen no longer advertises pass-and-play under the Single Player button.
Local multiplayer setup stays focused on Pass & play, so a one-device party table can never accidentally start a single-player run.
Desktop installers now load their bundled assets through relative paths, fixing the blank white window on Windows while the web build keeps its clean root-relative URLs.
Results copy is consistent: one-moment runs read '1 moment' instead of '1 moments', and a solo survivor who completes the whole archive sees 'You survived the archive'.
Mobile and desktop layouts keep every setup pill, scoreboard, and result inside the viewport bounds.

releases.title: Take the chronicle beyond the browser
releases.summary: Native desktop builds, late-join defaults, and touch-aware drag controls make every table easier to enter and play.
details: Time Chronicles now has a Tauri 2 desktop shell for Windows, macOS, and Linux while the installable web app remains available as the lightweight fallback.
The desktop chooser detects the player's operating system and offers Windows x64 NSIS, macOS universal DMG, or Linux x64 AppImage, Debian, and RPM packages when published.
Every installer entry includes its exact download size and SHA-256 checksum, and the release feed refuses duplicate, malformed, off-host, or mutable artifact paths.
A private multi-platform GitHub Actions build publishes only finished binaries and metadata to a dedicated public, binary-only GitHub Pages repository through a repository-scoped deploy key.
Unsigned preview builds remain free to distribute, with clear warnings that Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper can require confirmation until paid signing and notarization are configured.
The native shell sends multiplayer, reports, billing, weekly polls, live operations, and release-note requests to the production service instead of an unusable bundled relative API path.
External web, email, telephone, checkout, support, and source links open through the operating system, while executable protocols and untrusted installer metadata are rejected.
The desktop runtime skips the browser service worker and third-party AdSense script, uses bundled static assets, and keeps the existing PWA as a safe offline-capable fallback.
Join games in progress is now enabled by default for new Online and Nearby rooms; a host's explicit off choice still persists, hides the active room, and rejects late joins.
Solo, Chronicle, Local, Nearby, and Online hands now use one guarded drag system for mouse, pen, and touch input.
On phones, horizontal movement remains a swipeable hand carousel while a deliberate vertical gesture captures the card and moves it toward a glowing timeline gap.
Drag cancellation, disabled turns, automated turns, open results, handoffs, busy requests, and duplicate pointer completions cannot place a card accidentally or twice.
The public installer feed remains unavailable until real platform builds pass and publish, so players never see a placeholder download represented as a finished app.

releases.title: Keep every table in view
releases.summary: An always-visible release badge, host-controlled live-score privacy, explicit final reveals, and validated community controls keep every player oriented and every table deliberate.
details: The running version stays visible on every screen, including active games and dialogs, while modal spacing keeps the passive badge clear of player actions on narrow devices.
Hosts can show or hide live scores in Local, Solo, Chronicle, Nearby, and Online setup; the setting defaults on for existing tables and preserves an explicit off choice.
Hidden-score tables mask player totals, hand progress, per-play points, lives, streaks, elimination state, winner identity, and point-bearing result copy until final results are deliberately opened.
The final placement dialog no longer reveals the completed score early. Players choose See final results before exact totals appear.
Online room polling and placement responses redact score-bearing fields at the server boundary, so browser network tools cannot bypass the host's privacy choice.
A seated player's reconnect token can request authenticated final results only after the game is finished; unfinished and invalid requests are rejected.
Online progression reconciles the player's exact final score once and persists that reconciliation across refreshes and reconnects.
Show-live-scores travels through room creation, host updates, reconnects, standalone server parsing, and Nearby invites without changing other rules.
Staff can enable or disable the Monydragon Services Discord destination and enter a validated invite URL as free text.

Discord validation accepts only a canonical HTTPS discord.gg invite code and rejects credentials, ports, lookalike hosts, nested or dot-segment paths, queries, fragments, backslashes, controls, and encoded separators.
Disabled community links are omitted from public live operations and stay hidden during cold loads or service outages instead of flashing a stale default.
Staff and host settings now expose honest unapplied states, Apply and Discard behavior, failure-safe drafts, and navigation or browser-exit guards.
