Version, score-privacy, final-result, and community controls adapt to phones, safe areas, high contrast, large targets, keyboard focus, and screen readers.

releases.title: Give history a soundtrack
releases.summary: Five original generated music loops, ten responsive sound cues, a complete preview mixer, and an always-available mute control bring every kind of table to life.
details: Five deterministic procedural tracks — Quiet Archive, Clockwork Quiz, Lantern Library, Signal Room, and Starlit Timeline — are generated locally from original note recipes with no remote audio, licensing dependency, or tracking request.
Ten synthesized cues cover game start, card placement, correct answers, misses, turn changes, timer warnings, achievement unlocks, pack unlocks, room joins, and game completion.
Settings now includes independent master, music, and sound-effect controls, whole-number volume sliders, five explicit music previews, and all ten named effect previews.
Music selection and volume preferences stay on this device under their own safe, versioned audio setting and tolerate blocked or malformed browser storage.
A shared Mute / Unmute control stays easy to reach during play without becoming another independent floating bubble or covering ads, cards, dialogs, or phone safe areas.
Local, Solo, Chronicle, Nearby, and Online games share the same semantic audio path, including result, timer, progression, room, and final-score moments.
Online polling, placement retries, reconnects, joining in progress, stale responses, and play-again rounds are deduplicated so a sound never replays historical or repeated room activity.
Track previews stop after ten seconds, stop immediately when Settings closes or audio becomes unavailable, and restore the active game soundtrack when appropriate.
Browsers create and resume the audio graph only after a real pointer or keyboard gesture; hidden tabs fade, suspend, and resume only an already-unlocked session.
Track buffers, simultaneous effects, room cursors, and event keys are strictly bounded, while deterministic generation, crossfades, envelopes, peak limiting, and teardown protect mobile performance.
The mixer and shared dock support narrow phones, tablets, safe areas, high contrast, large targets, keyboard focus, live preview feedback, and screen-reader toggle semantics.

releases.title: Pull up a chair
releases.summary: The Monydragon Services community now has a prominent, accessible Discord entry point for players who want to meet, share, and follow what comes next.
details: A full-width community card on Home gives Discord a large, recognizable mark, clear invitation copy, and an easy-to-find Join on Discord action.
A compact footer link keeps the community discoverable after players move past the main card.
The canonical Monydragon Services invite is https://discord.gg/Y9uubFArnF and is centralized for reuse by future staff settings.
Every Discord link opens in a new tab with safe opener isolation and an explicit accessible name.
Player copy identifies Discord as an external service and makes clear that the independently operated Monydragon Services community is not affiliated with or endorsed by Discord.
Invite validation accepts only a bounded HTTPS discord.gg invite code and rejects lookalike hosts, credentials, ports, nested paths, query strings, fragments, backslashes, and encoded path tricks.
The community card adapts through narrow phone layouts and supports dark themes, high contrast, large touch targets, and visible keyboard focus.
The inline Discord mark is decorative because the surrounding text already names its destination, avoiding duplicate screen-reader announcements.

releases.title: Build the catalog, not the JSON
releases.summary: Staff gain a visual Catalog Studio for creating, organizing, previewing, marketing, publishing, and safely archiving decks and curated collections at scale.
details: Deck and collection directories now support search, status filters, useful sorts, compact summaries, and read-only references to every built-in deck.
A structured card workshop replaces raw JSON as the primary editor, with card search, category and difficulty filters, manual ordering, duplication, deletion, and field-level validation.
Editors can manage precise month, day, time, source label, and approved source URL fields while comparing spoiler-safe clue and revealed-card previews.
Featured placement, catalog order, search keywords, release labels, and staff-only campaign tags make packs and collections ready for discovery and marketing workflows.
Collections organize an intentional order of built-in and managed decks with add, remove, and reorder controls; publication refuses missing, draft, or archived managed decks.
Every edit remains local until Apply changes, with Discard actions, navigation and refresh guards, browser-exit protection, and honest reload-or-overwrite handling for revision conflicts.
Immutable slugs, reserved built-in identities, globally unique published card IDs, strict field validation, and atomic record-plus-history writes protect the playable catalog.
Publishing and archiving use dedicated recent-2FA actions and audit entries; a deck cannot be archived while a published collection still depends on it.
Revision histories provide read-only point-in-time snapshots for both decks and collections without turning old versions into destructive restore shortcuts.
Player-facing live operations expose only published catalog fields with stable IDs and revisions; drafts, archives, campaign tags, and staff actor details remain private.
Multiplayer now preserves managed-card month, day, time, and source labels with the same fidelity as local play.

releases.title: Every card shows its work
releases.summary: All 900 built-in cards now pass a canonical source audit, while players and staff gain a secure, review-only path for checking Wikipedia and other approved sources.
details: Every built-in deck now contains exactly 50 playable cards with globally unique IDs, preventing merge losses and metadata collisions.
A published, resumable source audit verifies all 900 card links and summaries against 775 canonical Wikipedia pages and records each page revision.
Twelve dead or renamed Wikipedia links were repaired and the server deck catalog was regenerated from the corrected source data.
The audit found 457 card years in their source summaries and places the remaining 443 into an explicit staff-review queue; a summary match is evidence, not an automatic date correction.
The player-facing See something off flow is now Check this card, available after reveal so it cannot bypass source-link point rules.

Wikipedia checks return a bounded canonical summary and revision snapshot; built-in Britannica, Library of Congress, Smithsonian, NASA, NOAA, National Archives, and UNESCO adapters return bounded page metadata.
Sources added by staff without a built-in adapter remain eligible for manual review and are never fetched automatically.
Every result only prefills a proposal for the support inbox. Players cannot directly update or publish a card.
Admins can manage approved source domains, and unsafe public suffixes, private hosts, IP addresses, credentials, ports, paths, and reserved domains are rejected.
Managed-pack source links and player correction links must match the active approved-source list.
Unrevealed hand-card reports omit date clues, while permanent source-validation errors stay visible instead of retrying forever as if the player were offline.

releases.title: One hundred ways to make history
releases.summary: Achievements expand to 100 goals, while host rule controls gain consistent mobile layout, broad presets, validated custom values, and deliberate Apply/Discard handling.
details: The achievement collection now contains exactly 100 unique goals spanning games, wins, placements, accuracy, points, streaks, timelines, decks, modes, and Solo, Local, and Online play.
Every room-rule row now uses consistent alignment, spacing, borders, and mobile sizing.
Score and streak targets offer many presets plus validated custom whole numbers from 3 through 1,000,000,000 instead of stopping at deck size.
Turn and disconnected-player timers include expanded presets and validated custom values up to 24 hours.
Room-rule edits remain a local draft until the host chooses Apply changes, with a visible unsaved state and a Discard action.
Local setup also supports preset and custom score and timer values.

releases.title: Customize closes cleanly
releases.summary: Fixed the floating Customize panel so its close control exits the popover and restores the shortcut reliably.
details: Closing the floating Customize panel now removes the panel instead of leaving it rendered over the page.
The floating Customize shortcut returns after closing, ready to reopen the appearance controls.
The fix preserves all mode, color, typography, and accessibility choices.

releases.title: Settings put customization in one place
releases.summary: Appearance controls now live with Settings, while the floating Customize button is an explicit opt-in and stays off by default.
details: The home menu now combines Customize with Settings so appearance controls have one clear destination.
Settings includes a Floating Customize button toggle for players who prefer a quick overlay shortcut.
The floating Customize shortcut defaults to Off and remains hidden until enabled.
The preference is saved locally on the device and is included in Reset reading & access settings.
When enabled, the floating shortcut opens the same appearance panel for mode, accent, background, text, and accessibility choices.

releases.title: Solo play stays in the moment
releases.summary: Solo and Chronicle games now begin and continue without pass-the-device handoff screens, and a failed run stays on its completed result until the player chooses what comes next.
details: Solo runs open directly on the playable hand without a Ready hand confirmation.
Chronicle challenge also skips Ready hand confirmations because only one human is using the device.
The hand-visibility privacy setting now appears only for multi-human Pass & play tables, where hiding the next player's cards is useful.
Pass & play and Nearby games with multiple people retain Reveal on turn handoffs when configured.
Dismissing the final placement result reveals the final-results screen without creating another game.
A failed Solo run preserves its game identity, earlier correct plays, score, timeline, and complete move history.
Play Again remains the only action that creates a fresh Solo or Chronicle game; Return home remains the separate exit choice.

releases.title: See what players know
releases.summary: Staff analytics now explain which packs and categories are played, average results, common card misses and successes, and broader game-mode behavior.
details: Completed games now contribute pack-selection, mode, context, card count, points, accuracy, category, and per-card result summaries.
Online completion summaries come from the authoritative room game history, including results hidden from other players by room display settings.
Local and Solo completions send a bounded best-effort anonymous summary; telemetry failures never interrupt or delay a game.
The staff Analytics page shows total placements, correct and missed cards, average accuracy, average cards per game, and average points per game.
Pack usage ranks selected packs by completed games and reports the combined result for games in which each pack appeared.
Category tables show play volume and correct, missed, and accuracy results for every chronology category.
Separate rankings identify the most commonly missed and most commonly correct cards, including their play counts and accuracy.
Context and game-mode panels compare how often Solo, Local, and Online tables and the five rule sets are completed.
Player names are never included; custom deck identifiers collapse to Custom and custom card titles collapse to Custom card before leaving the device.
Incoming summaries are same-origin, rate-limited, size-capped, allowlisted, and retained under the existing analytics expiry policy.

releases.title: Put a password on your table
releases.summary: Hosts can optionally protect public and hidden Online rooms with a password while saved player seats continue to reconnect without repeated prompts.
details: Room setup now accepts an optional 4–72 character password for public, invite-only, and private Online rooms.
Joining by code includes a password field, and password-protected public rooms show a clear Locked marker before a player tries to enter.
Selecting a protected public room fills its room code and asks for the password instead of making a guaranteed-to-fail join request.
Passwords are transformed with a unique random salt and a deliberately slow scrypt hash before durable storage; plaintext is never retained or returned to players.
Missing and incorrect passwords receive the same rejection, and excessively long join attempts are refused before password hashing.
Existing rooms and password-free rooms continue to work exactly as before.
A player who has already joined resumes with the saved reconnect token, so an app close or network drop does not force another password entry.
Protected private and invite-only rooms remain absent from the public room browser and are still reachable only through a shared code.

releases.title: Rooms clean up after themselves
releases.summary: Online room lifecycle rules now remove abandoned lobbies, absent games, stalled running games, and completed tables while preserving active and reconnecting players.
details: Empty waiting rooms automatically clear after 15 minutes without a present player.
Games with nobody present retain a six-hour reconnect window before their room is removed.
A running game with no turn or gameplay progress clears after 12 hours even if a stale browser resumes polling.
Finished rooms remain available for a one-hour results review, then clear automatically.
Any genuinely active turn updates the gameplay clock, so active tables are not mistaken for stalled rooms.
Authorized staff can still remove one exact room immediately or preview and confirm a bulk inactive-room cleanup.
Bulk cleanup protects games in progress by default; including them requires an explicit reason, recent 2FA, and an audit record.
The staff room page now states every automatic lifecycle threshold beside the live directory.

releases.title: Every collection opens up
releases.summary: The Deck Builder now previews complete collections and gives players precise controls for finding, sorting, choosing, and modifying their cards.
details: Every unlocked built-in, managed, weekly, or custom collection opens a complete card browser before game setup.
Search within a collection by card title, description, or category and filter by category or Easy, Medium, and Hard difficulty.
Sort the card browser by original deck order, title, oldest first, or newest first, with accurate matching-card counts.
Collection-level search, category filters, card-count sorting, A–Z sorting, and newest-custom sorting remain available on the main shelf.
Custom collections expose edit, duplicate, export, and confirmation-protected delete actions inside their preview.
Empty card filters have a clear recovery action, and the browser adapts from four controls to a single-column phone layout.
A dedicated Use this deck action keeps browsing separate from starting a game.

releases.title: The table fits the screen
releases.summary: Mobile play now keeps a compact timeline and swipeable hand in view, while clearer direction, timers, and Chronicle difficulty improve every table.
details: Phone timeline cards shrink to a stable, anchored rail and omit descriptions after placement so the chronology stays readable without taking over the screen.
Hands are horizontal swipe carousels with snap points; touch swipes scroll instead of starting a drag, while tapping still selects a card.
The mobile game title, turn status, timeline, gaps, and hand use a compact single-pane layout with consistent insertion-point height.
Older and Newer labels now mark the two ends of every timeline, and the first insertion point aligns with every later gap on desktop and mobile.
Customize moved into the home menu instead of floating over play, while the full appearance panel remains available on demand.
Chronicle challenge replaces the vague versus-AI wording and offers Casual, Balanced, and Expert accuracy settings.
Only Time Attack uses timer-focused headings, and its live seconds remain visible beside the shared timeline.

releases.title: Updates and decks stay easy to explore
releases.summary: The desktop changelog now scrolls correctly, while every game setup has a searchable, filterable deck selector with clear descriptions and card previews.
details: The changelog keeps its header and Dismiss action visible while the release history scrolls inside a dedicated desktop and mobile region.
Opening release notes locks background page movement, supports Escape, and restores the previous page state when closed.
Deck and pack selection can be searched by name, story, description, or category and filtered to a specific category.
Every visible deck has a stable, non-overlapping card with its card count, categories, and short pack description.
A dedicated Preview cards action opens eight spoiler-safe sample cards without revealing their dates.
The selector uses a single-column phone layout and a bounded, touch-friendly scroll region so the complete catalog remains discoverable.

releases.title: Staff can guide the live game
releases.summary: Authorized staff can now pause or restore individual player features from Global settings without shipping another build.
details: Twelve switches cover release notices, achievements, the weekly poll, the Pack Store, previews, point unlocks, donations, future Stripe packs, late joins, reconnectable seats, away-player skipping, and source-link penalties.
Feature changes are protected by the existing staff permission, CSRF, and recent-authenticator checks and are recorded in the audit log.
Online players refresh live-operations settings every minute, so player-facing entry points respond without requiring a new deployment.
Room setup and host editing hide disabled room rules and force them off in newly submitted room settings.
Paused Store, preview, donation, poll, achievement, release-notice, and source-warning experiences disappear cleanly while saved progress and room data remain intact.
Every switch defaults to on, preserving the current game until authorized staff deliberately changes it.

releases.title: Find and preview your next story
releases.summary: The Store is now a searchable pack catalog with spoiler-safe previews and clear point, donation, and future Stripe paths.
details: Search pack names, story descriptions, and category labels from one catalog field.
Filter the shelf by category or by All, Locked, Owned, and Ready now unlock states.
Preview six sample cards from any pack without revealing their dates or chronology clues.
Locked packs show their point cost and remaining balance, and become directly unlockable when enough points are available.
Future per-pack Stripe checkout is visible but remains disabled until the verified paid catalog launches.
Donation links lead to the PayPal support options and explicitly explain that donations do not automatically unlock a current pack.

releases.title: More story on every playable card
releases.summary: Playable cards now carry a concise chronology-safe description, supported by a more unified type, color, focus, and control system.
details: Local and Online hand cards show the card's short clue beneath its title before placement.
Temporal clues remain scrubbed from playable descriptions so the hidden date stays part of the game.
Descriptions use a consistent three-line layout that keeps hands readable on desktop, mobile, and enlarged-text settings.
Shared surface, subtle-text, border, and focus tokens now drive playable cards and form controls across light, dark, and custom themes.
Selected-card descriptions, date rows, and info controls now derive contrast from the active theme instead of fixed colors.

releases.title: The game now stops at the ending
releases.summary: Single-player runs always show their final results and wait for a clear replay choice instead of jumping into another game.
details: The last card's result remains visible until the player chooses to continue to the final summary.
Finishing a Solo or versus-Chronicle game can no longer call the new-game action from the result modal.
The final summary now remains the only place where Try again or Play again can start a fresh run.
Returning home is always available beside the replay choice.
A regression test protects the result-to-summary-to-replay sequence.

releases.title: Your chronicle has milestones
releases.summary: Achievements, live unlock notices, and guided goals now turn Solo, Local, and Online statistics into a shared progression journey.
details: Fifteen achievements cover first steps, wins, accuracy, points, streaks, long timelines, game modes, categories, decks, and ways to play.
Dedicated milestones recognize Solo challenges, Local multiplayer tables, and Online multiplayer rooms.
Newly earned achievements appear immediately in a dismissible in-game notice and keep their unlock date on this device.
The Stats screen now includes a complete achievement collection plus the three closest goals with live progress bars.
Online game completion is recorded for every player who reaches the finished table, and reconnecting cannot count the same result twice.

releases.title: Keep every turn moving fairly
releases.summary: Hosts can opt into an away-player skip timer and decide whether opening a playable card's source forfeits its points.
details: Disconnected-player skipping is off by default and can be configured by the host from 15 seconds to 5 minutes.
An away skip advances the turn without consuming the absent player's card or recording a missed answer.
Opening a source from a playable hand card now shows a clear confirmation that the card will lose its points if placed correctly.
The source penalty is enabled by default, can be disabled by the host, and is enforced by the multiplayer server rather than trusting the browser.
Local, solo, versus-Chronicle, Nearby, and Online setup surfaces all use the same source-warning rule.

releases.title: Come back to the same table
releases.summary: Hosts can open active games to new players, while reconnectable seats remain protected by default.
details: Hosts can choose whether new players may join after a game has started.
Rejoining after an app close or network interruption is enabled by default and can be configured by the host.
Public in-progress rooms appear in the room browser only when the host allows late joins.
Every release now has a dismissible player-facing update notice and a detailed changelog available from Home.
Players already online are prompted when a newer deployed version is detected and can reload when ready.

releases.title: A support inbox staff can actually use
releases.summary: Support requests and card feedback arrive in one filterable dashboard where staff can assign, prioritize, track, and resolve reports while replies route through the configured support address.
details: Support requests and card feedback land in a single filterable staff inbox with assignment, priority, status, private notes, replies, and resolution.
support@monydragon.com is the default destination and authorized staff can change it from Global settings; public support links follow the configured address.
The staff login and dashboard gain system, light, and dark themes plus custom colors, typography, reduced motion, high contrast, and larger targets.

releases.title: The host's table is the table
releases.summary: Hosts govern the merged deck, disconnected players pause their turn, optional turn clocks are server-authoritative, and first-time players follow their device theme.
details: The host's selected packs and merged card total now govern the whole room, so guests can ready and play without owning those packs locally.
Disconnected players pause their turn instead of being silently skipped, while explicit departures and removals publish a clear reason.
Hosts can choose off, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, or 120 second turn limits; server-authoritative timeouts are announced to everyone and never award points.
First-time players follow their device theme until they explicitly choose Light or Dark.

releases.title: An invite-only staff console
releases.summary: A secure /staff console with owner setup, TOTP 2FA, role-based permissions, room operations, pack authoring, and a hardened OAuth flow launches behind MongoDB.
details: The owner creates the first password with a high-entropy one-time setup code or verified Google identity, then enrolls TOTP 2FA and saves backup codes.
Owner, admin, moderator, author, analyst, and partner roles use server-enforced permissions; authorized staff invite teammates and manage roles, status, 2FA resets, and the audit trail.
Staff can monitor players, rooms, analytics, and activity; clean up inactive rooms; publish announcements; and control maintenance, registration, and room limits.
Authors create and revise sourced packs, while publishing requires the publish permission and a recent 2FA check; published packs are pinned into active room snapshots.
Local, Online, and Nearby rooms support up to 32 players, with 2–16 recommended, deck-aware table-size validation, and large-roster layouts.

releases.title: Hands reveal on your turn
releases.summary: Hosts can keep every waiting hand blank until its turn begins, and choose between Standard or Draw hand flow with independent visibility rules.
details: Reveal-on-turn hands hide card details on the server until the exact moment a turn begins.
Draw mode starts with one card, replenishes on correct plays, and draws one to four host-selected replacements after a miss.
Standard or Draw flow combines with Ready Hand or Reveal on Turn visibility in Local and Online setup, and Nearby invites preserve the same rules.

releases.title: The community builds the next pack
releases.summary: A weekly home-screen poll chooses a 50-card community pack automatically, while card feedback and the player support form make corrections and help easy to send.
details: The weekly poll opens with a player-powered spotlight on Home; one vote per device, up to three ideas per participant, and a bounded 100-entry board.
The highest-voted idea becomes a named 50-card pack selected deterministically from the sourced catalog and released automatically on the configured schedule.
Every card and post-play result offers a See something off action for dates, names, descriptions, sources, disambiguation, and other issues.
The Support screen includes an accessible help form that opens a pre-filled email to support@monydragon.com.
Light and dark canvases now preserve the shared theme background across every screen, and scaled text viewports no longer expose a white strip.

releases.title: Ads fall back gracefully
releases.summary: Whenever the online AdSense slot reports no fill, is blocked, or fails, the Monydragon Services sponsor appears in the same banner instead of an empty box.
details: The automatic sponsor fallback keeps the same dismiss and Go ad-free actions, and ad-free entitlements still remove the entire banner.
The manual AdSense unit stays in normal document flow, never floats over content, and stays gated by local entitlements.

releases.title: Policy-safe ads
releases.summary: The supplied AdSense footer slot renders in a persistent normal-flow banner instead of a floating box, while ad-free entitlements remain protected.
details: The Google slot and publisher meta tag live in the app shell, while the placement renders only after billing and ad-free entitlements are checked.
Verified subscriptions, lifetime access, PayPal donations, and earned ad-free rewards remove the Google placement entirely.
/ads.txt remains available at the site root for AdSense review.

releases.title: An ad rail that respects the game
releases.summary: A persistent responsive footer banner replaces floating ads, with honest loading diagnostics and full ad-free protection.
details: The Footer_Banner slot renders in a persistent normal-flow banner on desktop, mobile, and game views, never as a floating overlay.
The rail stays visibly reserved while Google loads or returns no fill, with clear status for review, inventory, and ad-blocking conditions.
Subscription, lifetime, PayPal donation, and earned ad-free entitlements remove the entire rail.

releases.title: Support the chronicle
releases.summary: PayPal donations grant temporary ad-free time by tier, Stripe stays clearly coming soon, and a quick tutorial explains the whole game.
details: PayPal donations link directly to monydragon@gmail.com with $0.99/1 day through $49.99/1 year ad-free tiers; the one-year tier is marked best value.
After donating, players confirm their tier on-device for temporary ad-free time; the bridge is clearly labeled temporary until receipt verification is added.
A short data-driven tutorial covers modes, placement, results, Collections versus Store, accessibility, Stats, and offline play.

releases.title: Earn first
releases.summary: Five free 50-card packs, a play-to-earn points economy, temporary ad-free redemptions, and an honest pre-1.0 soft launch arrive together.
details: Fresh profiles start with Foundations, Signals, After Hours, Wild World, and Makers Lab; Collections show only unlocked packs and the Store lists every locked path.
Every played card counts toward points, including misses; the cadence is configurable and a 50-card pack costs 25 points.
Players can spend 75 points for a week, 250 for a month, or 2,500 for a year of ad-free play, plus claim one free month before 1.0.
Stripe paid unlocks remain disabled until checkout, webhook, cancellation, and restore verification is complete.

releases.title: Monydragon credits and verified unlocks
releases.summary: A small labeled sponsor links to Monydragon, while a $2.99/month or $9.99 one-time Stripe path unlocks the current catalog with durable recovery codes.
details: The free edition carries a clearly labeled Monydragon Services sponsor with links to monydragon.com and its services page.
The $2.99/month subscription or $9.99 one-time purchase removes the sponsor and unlocks every current pack after server verification.
Future packs stay separate $0.50 add-ons, and recovery codes restore verified access on another device.
Server-only Stripe REST calls create checkout sessions while signed webhooks persist entitlements in the durable backend.

releases.title: Nearby stays on hold
releases.summary: The Multiplayer explorer keeps a visible Nearby tab labeled Coming soon, so unfinished Bluetooth prompts never reach players.
details: Nearby is disabled behind a release flag that prevents capability checks, permission prompts, scans, joins, and bridge handoff.
An old Nearby route opens a Coming Soon screen instead of a partially released flow.
Local pass-and-play and Online hosted rooms remain active.

releases.title: Nearby handoff made explicit
releases.summary: Active Nearby rooms open a guided share/setup dialog, and first-time Bluetooth scans handle Android scan-response quirks reliably.
details: A dedicated share dialog shows the room code, native share/copy actions, a manual invite link, and step-by-step bridge and guest instructions.
The Web Bluetooth chooser uses acceptAllDevices with the Time Chronicles service as an optional service for Android scan-response quirks.
The Android bridge keeps the service in the primary advertisement and the phone name in scan-response data.

releases.title: Reliable two-device discovery
releases.summary: Nearby scans approved hosts in parallel with timeouts, reconnects GATT links before writes, and fixes the end-screen layout.
details: An explicit Scan now action plus automatic getDevices() refreshes connect remembered hosts independently and in parallel.
The browser reconnects an approved device before a join or state packet and times out stalled GATT operations with recovery text.
The Android bridge serves compact raw-JSON invites, caps read responses to MTU-1, and buffers prepared long writes.
Winner, resolution, and handoff panels scroll within the viewport on desktop and mobile.

releases.title: Bluetooth rooms you can join
releases.summary: Discovered Nearby room cards open straight into the join flow with the host's deck and rules, and the Android bridge contract is documented.
details: A discovered Bluetooth room card opens the join flow instead of a generic Nearby screen, sending the guest's name through the join characteristic.
Nearby hosts choose decks, Classic or Survival rules, score, hearts, recycling, hints, action visibility, dates, and card info before hosting.
The bridge advertises the documented service and invite characteristic and accepts guest joins.

releases.title: Automatic Bluetooth lobby scan
releases.summary: The Nearby tab re-checks already-approved devices and lists valid room invites without a surprise permission chooser.
details: Automatic getDevices() scans list valid Time Chronicles room invites from devices the player already approved.
Scan Bluetooth rooms remains the explicit first-connection action; afterward automatic scans reconnect to remembered devices.
